title: Deep-learning based Cardiac Disease classification, Interpretation and Outcome prediction
summary:
Cardiovascular diseases are among the leading causes of death worldwide. Imaging techniques such as cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cardiac MRI) and echocardiography (heart ultrasound) are used to detect them at an early stage and assess their progression. These examinations provide highly detailed images of the beating heart; until now, the interpretation of these images has mostly been carried out manually or semi-automatically – a process that is time-consuming and can vary depending on the examiner.
In this study, pseudonymised image data from cardiac MRI and echocardiography, along with associated findings and clinical information (e.g. age, gender, pre-existing conditions), which were generated as part of routine clinical care at Heidelberg University Hospital, are being retrospectively analysed. The aim is to develop and test computer-aided machine learning methods (artificial intelligence) that can automatically divide the cardiac cycle into its individual phases and automatically calculate the movement and deformation of the heart muscle (known as ‘strain’). These values are considered promising early indicators of various heart conditions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Performance of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cardiac MRI) and/or echocardiography at the Department of Internal Medicine III – Cardiology, Angiology and Pneumology at Heidelberg University Hospital between 2006 and 2024, regardless of the underlying cardiovascular diagnosis or clinical issue
Exclusion criteria:
- An existing pregnancy at the time of the examination
- Express objection by the patient to the scientific (secondary) use of their data, provided such an objection is documented
- Image or findings data that cannot be analysed or are technically inadequate (e.g. significant motion artefacts, incomplete image sequences, insufficient temporal resolution for determining cardiac phases)
